assessments.reasoning: The LENGTH section on printed page 50 describes counting the evaluated result in bytes after symbolic substitution and applicable arithmetic. Its arithmetic example counts the two digits in eleven rather than the five source characters.

challenge.method: Recomputed the example sum and result length, then compared the STR-protected input, double-byte character example, and SYSCLENGTH contrast on printed page 51.
challenge.results: The additive expression gives decimal 11 and two single-byte digits. STR makes the example count five source characters without evaluating the arithmetic. The DBCS and SYSCLENGTH paragraphs confirm distinct byte and character counting.

limitations: The qualifier applicable preserves the STR control. The result does not establish Unicode handling or an observed runtime.
